maria_support: Customer sees 401 when calling generate, says they can't find any request id in their app logs. They’re non-technical — need a tiny checklist I can paste. :wave:

devin_eng: Super short checklist for non-devs: 1) Take a screenshot of the browser/devtool network response headers (if web). 2) Copy the timestamp + timezone when the error happened. 3) If they have Console access, generate a debug snapshot and send the token. 4) If they can run one command, run a simple curl and paste output.

sophia_se: Add ask for SDK name + version (we often see older SDKs that mask headers). Also ask whether they use a proxy or corporate firewall.

maria_support: If they can only send one thing, what should it be?

devin_eng: One thing = screenshot of network response headers that shows the status and response headers. If the screenshot shows a header like `x-rw-request-id` or `x-request-id` include that exact string. If screenshot not possible, send the debug token from Console sessions.

anna_support: Steps for Console debug token (copy-paste to send to customers):
1) Go to Console -> Sessions
2) Filter by email or approximate time
3) Click the session -> Snapshot -> Generate Debug Token
4) Send the token string (starts with `dbg_`) to support

sophia_se: For mobile SDKs: ask them to enable debug logging (we provide a single-line toggle) or show them the callback where `requestRef` is surfaced. Example log lines we look for: `rw_req: <id>` or `trace: <trace_id>`.

devin_eng: Minimal curl to ask them to paste (tell them to redact auth token):
```
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"test"}'
```
Mention: include the full verbatim response headers and body.

maria_support: They said the header isn't present in responses. Any other spots to check?

sophia_se: Check SDK-level logs first. If they use a CDN or reverse proxy, that layer sometimes rewrites or strips headers — ask them to check upstream logs for `x-request-id`. Also ask for the exact region they hit (us-east-1, eu-west-1, etc.).

anna_support: Copy-paste message for customers (short):
"Hi — to help debug please send ONE of the following: a) Screenshot of the network response showing headers and status, b) A debug token from Console (Console -> Sessions -> Snapshot -> Generate Debug Token), or c) a pasted curl response (Authorization redacted). Also include the time (ISO) and SDK/platform version if known"

devin_eng: If we get a debug token we can map it to internal traces and return the service-side `x-rw-request-id` or trace info. If they can’t provide that, ask for a minimal reproducible payload (1-2 prompts) and whether they used Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

maria_support: Great, I'll send that. Thanks! :thumbsup:
